title: Cast brass head with beaded crown (side and front views)
creator: Benin court brass-casters (object); unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Photographs of objects printed in a book published in 1900. The objects themselves are centuries old.
original_holder: Augustus Pitt-Rivers, Antique Works of Art from Benin (London: privately printed, 1900), via Project Gutenberg #44014 (Figs. 82-83). The object was taken from Benin City by the British expedition of 1897.
caption: A cast head wearing a net-like beaded crown with strands hanging to the shoulders, shown in profile and from the front. The 1900 catalogue calls it the head of a woman. Heads like this are often linked to the Queen Mother (Iyoba). The catalogue's own wording reflects the racial language of its time.

title: Cast brass commemorative head (side and front views)
creator: Benin court brass-casters (object); unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Photographs of objects printed in a book published in 1900. The objects themselves are centuries old.
original_holder: Augustus Pitt-Rivers, Antique Works of Art from Benin (London: privately printed, 1900), via Project Gutenberg #44014 (Figs. 94-95). The object was taken from Benin City by the British expedition of 1897.
caption: A brass head with a high collar of coral beads and a beaded cap, with three raised marks above each eye. The pupils are inlaid with iron. Heads like this stood on royal altars to honour past Obas. This one is shown from the side and from the front.

title: Brass figure of a European with a matchlock gun (two views)
creator: Benin court brass-casters (object); unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Photographs of objects printed in a book published in 1900. The objects themselves are centuries old.
original_holder: Augustus Pitt-Rivers, Antique Works of Art from Benin (London: privately printed, 1900), via Project Gutenberg #44014 (Figs. 84-85). The object was taken from Benin City by the British expedition of 1897.
caption: A bearded European in a brimmed hat aiming a gun, whose barrel has broken off. Benin artists had been portraying Portuguese traders and soldiers since the 1500s. Here Europeans are the people being watched and recorded, not the ones recording.

title: The Eiffel Tower at the time of the Universal Exposition of 1889
creator: Engraving by Poyet (signed) for La Nature
why_public_domain: Wood engraving printed in La Nature in 1889; reproduced in a 1961 Smithsonian (US government) publication.
original_holder: Robert M. Vogel, Elevator Systems of the Eiffel Tower, 1889 (Smithsonian Institution, United States National Museum Bulletin 228, 1961), via Project Gutenberg #32282, reproducing the French magazine La Nature (1889) (Fig. 1)
caption: The new tower above the exhibition grounds, with the domed palaces of the Exposition at its feet. It was printed in the popular science weekly La Nature in June 1889, a few weeks after the fair opened.

title: The promenade beneath the Eiffel Tower, 1889
creator: Unknown engraver for La Nature
why_public_domain: Wood engraving printed in La Nature in 1889; reproduced in a 1961 Smithsonian (US government) publication.
original_holder: Robert M. Vogel, Elevator Systems of the Eiffel Tower, 1889 (Smithsonian Institution, United States National Museum Bulletin 228, 1961), via Project Gutenberg #32282, reproducing the French magazine La Nature (1889) (Fig. 6)
caption: Visitors stroll under the tower's great arch toward the central dome of the exhibition. The tower worked as a gateway to the fair, and the crowds came through it.

title: Lift machinery and passenger platforms at the tower's second level
creator: Unknown engraver for La Nature
why_public_domain: Wood engraving printed in La Nature in 1889; reproduced in a 1961 Smithsonian (US government) publication.
original_holder: Robert M. Vogel, Elevator Systems of the Eiffel Tower, 1889 (Smithsonian Institution, United States National Museum Bulletin 228, 1961), via Project Gutenberg #32282, reproducing the French magazine La Nature (1889) (Fig. 30)
caption: High in the tower, an American-built Otis lift arrives at the second-level platform beside a spiral staircase. Visitors crowd the landings. This is the 1889 fair as a machine people could ride.

title: Passengers changing lift cars halfway up the tower
creator: Engraving signed Poyet, for La Nature
why_public_domain: Wood engraving printed in La Nature in 1889; reproduced in a 1961 Smithsonian (US government) publication.
original_holder: Robert M. Vogel, Elevator Systems of the Eiffel Tower, 1889 (Smithsonian Institution, United States National Museum Bulletin 228, 1961), via Project Gutenberg #32282, reproducing the French magazine La Nature (1889) (Fig. 39)
caption: In top hats and bonnets, passengers cross from one Edoux lift car to the other on a small platform halfway up the tower's top section. La Nature printed this two days before the Exposition opened.

title: Calvary (The Green Christ / Breton Calvary)
creator: Paul Gauguin
why_public_domain: Painted in 1889. Gauguin died in 1903. Reproduced in a book published in New York in 1921.
original_holder: John Gould Fletcher, Paul Gauguin: His Life and Art (New York: Nicholas L. Brown, 1921), via Project Gutenberg #38848; original painting in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels
caption: Gauguin painted this in Brittany in 1889, the year he saw the exhibition's colonial villages in Paris. A Breton woman sits at the foot of a weathered stone calvary, which shows the body of Christ held by three women. This is a black-and-white reproduction from 1921, so the green of the title cannot be seen.

title: Self-portrait
creator: Vincent van Gogh
date: Paris period, c. 1886-1888 (the book gives no date)
why_public_domain: Van Gogh died in 1890. Reproduced as the frontispiece of a book published in 1913.
original_holder: The Letters of a Post-Impressionist, trans. Anthony M. Ludovici (Boston and New York: Houghton Mifflin, 1913), via Project Gutenberg #40393
caption: Van Gogh as he painted himself in Paris, shown in a black-and-white plate from 1913. In 1889, the year of the Exposition, he was in the asylum at Saint-Rémy and could only read about the fair in Theo's letters.

title: Wheat field with a cypress (drawing)
creator: Vincent van Gogh
date: probably 1889 (the book gives no title or date)
why_public_domain: Van Gogh died in 1890. Reproduced in a book published in 1913.
original_holder: The Letters of a Post-Impressionist, trans. Anthony M. Ludovici (Boston and New York: Houghton Mifflin, 1913), plate facing p. 200, via Project Gutenberg #40393
caption: A wheat field in a storm of short pen strokes, with a tall cypress and village roofs behind. The 1913 book prints it without a title or date. Its subject and style match Van Gogh's Saint-Rémy drawings of 1889, but that dating is ours, not the book's.

title: 'Wayang dancers'
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Photograph published in London in 1905. The photographer is not named.
original_holder: Augusta de Wit, Java: Facts and Fancies (London: Chapman & Hall, 1905), via Project Gutenberg #43665
caption: Four young Javanese dancers in crowns and court costume, captioned only 'Wayang dancers'. This is NOT a confirmed photograph of the troupe at the 1889 Paris fair, and the book names no one. It shows the kind of court dance that astonished Debussy and other visitors to the Kampong Javanais that year.

title: Rabindranath Tagore, from the portrait in colours by Sasi Kumar Hesh
creator: Sasi Kumar Hesh
why_public_domain: Published in New York in 1917, so PD in the US. We have not verified the artist's death date, so worldwide status is unconfirmed (he is generally said to have died around 1917).
original_holder: Rabindranath Tagore, My Reminiscences (New York: Macmillan, 1917), via Project Gutenberg #22217 (frontispiece)
caption: Tagore in his fifties, grey-bearded and looking to one side, drawn in pastel on grey paper. It was the colour frontispiece of his memoir in the West, four years after the Nobel Prize made him famous there.

title: Rabindranath Tagore in 1877
creator: Signed sketch dated 1877, probably by his elder brother Jyotirindranath Tagore
why_public_domain: Drawing dated 1877. Jyotirindranath Tagore died in 1925. Published in 1917.
original_holder: Rabindranath Tagore, My Reminiscences (New York: Macmillan, 1917), via Project Gutenberg #22217
caption: Tagore at about sixteen, in profile, in a quick dark sketch signed and dated 1877. Thirty-five years later he would be in London with the manuscript of Gitanjali. The book captions it only 'Rabindranath Tagore in 1877'. Our attribution to Jyotirindranath rests on the signature and his known portrait sketches of the family.

title: 'The Inner Garden was My Paradise'
creator: Gaganendranath Tagore
why_public_domain: Published in 1917. Gaganendranath Tagore died in 1938, so the work is PD in India (life + 60), the EU (life + 70) and the US (published before 1929).
original_holder: Rabindranath Tagore, My Reminiscences (New York: Macmillan, 1917), via Project Gutenberg #22217
caption: Gaganendranath Tagore, the poet's nephew, painted this view through an arched doorway into the garden of the Tagore house in Calcutta, where Rabindranath spent his childhood. It is a soft ink-wash picture of the world that Gitanjali's quiet images grew out of.

title: Mei Lan-fang: in European dress and in three roles
creator: Unknown photographers
why_public_domain: Published in the United States in 1925, so PD in the US (pre-1929). The photographers are not named. China protects published photographs for 50 years, so these have very probably expired there too, but worldwide status is unconfirmed.
original_holder: A. E. Zucker, The Chinese Theater (Boston: Little, Brown, 1925), via Project Gutenberg #69475
caption: Four photographs on one plate. Mei Lanfang stands in a Western suit, then appears in three of his dan (female) roles: 'Ch'ang-O's Flight to the Moon', 'Burying the Blossoms' and 'A Young Nun Seeks Love'. They were printed a decade before his 1935 visit to Moscow.

title: A typical Peking theater
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Published in the United States in 1925, so PD in the US (pre-1929). The photographer is not named, so worldwide status is unconfirmed.
original_holder: A. E. Zucker, The Chinese Theater (Boston: Little, Brown, 1925), via Project Gutenberg #69475
caption: A crowded Peking playhouse in the 1920s, with lanterns hanging over an open thrust stage and spectators seated close on three sides. This is the kind of house Mei Lanfang played in at home.

title: The orchestra seated in a corner of the stage
creator: Alexandre Jacovleff (Aleksandr Yakovlev)
why_public_domain: Painting published in Jacovleff's 'Le Théâtre chinois' (1922) and reproduced in the US in 1925, so PD in the US. Jacovleff died in 1938, so the work is also PD in countries with life + 70 or shorter terms.
original_holder: A. E. Zucker, The Chinese Theater (Boston: Little, Brown, 1925), via Project Gutenberg #69475, reproduced from Jacovleff, Le Théâtre chinois (1922)
caption: The Russian painter Alexandre Jacovleff watched Peking opera around 1919 and painted its musicians playing gongs, clappers and fiddles beside the actors. Thirteen years later, Moscow audiences would hear this sound when Mei Lanfang came to perform.
